messages.author: Godbole, Shivani
messages.body:
Hello,
This is Shivani Godbole. I am a student at Penn State University. I have been trying to download AMBER for the last two days and I am having issues doing so. I was wondering if you could help me out with that. I am trying to download cmake to install AMBER, but it is just not working. I downloaded cmake and installed it but its not working.
Please let me know if you have any suggestions as to what I should do.
Thank you,
Shivani Sujay Godbole
Biomedical Sciences
Penn State College of Medicine

messages.author: Todd Minehardt
messages.body:
Shivani,
If you have a problem downloading AMBER - and not AmberTools - that's
likely a license issue.
However, since you then state that you're having problems with cmake while
trying to install AMBER, I'm going to assume you have succeeded in
downloading it.
The AMBER Manual has a rather complete installation description.
Additionally, you can search this mailing list archive and find pretty much
anything relevant.
You'll need to provide way more information to us if we are to be of any
help: operating system, GPU (or not), and so on.
Cheers,
Todd

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Jan 26, 2024, Godbole, Shivani via AMBER wrote:
>This is Shivani Godbole. I am a student at Penn State University. I have
>been trying to download AMBER for the last two days and I am having
>issues doing so. I was wondering if you could help me out with that. I am
>trying to download cmake to install AMBER, but it is just not working. I
>downloaded cmake and installed it but its not working.
Just to expand a bit on previous answers.  Saying "it's not working" doesn't
allow any one to help.  You will need to say exactly what you tried, and
exactly what happened.  (For example, we don't even know what operating
system you are using.)
As noted earlier, we also don't know if the problem is with the download, or
with the subsequent installation procedure.  Be sure to visit
https://ambermd.org/Installation.php
, and go to the page that corresponds to
your operating system.  There is often useful information there.
...good luck...dac
